category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO fracture classification, what do the frst and second digits represent?
back:
• First digit: Identifes the specifc bone.
• Second digit: Identifes the segment (1-Proximal, 2-Diaphysis, 3-Distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: prox - imal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does the AO system categorize the 'Type' (Letter) of diaphyseal fractures?
back:
• A: Simple fracture (complete contact >95%).
• B: Wedge fracture (partial contact).
• C: Multifragmentary/Segmental (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [A – After reduction complete contact... B – After reduction partial contact... C – After reduction no contact... (segmental)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO metaphyseal fracture Types B and C regarding articular involvement.
back:
• Type B (Partial articular): Part of the joint surface remains attached to the diaphysis.
• Type C (Complete articular): Articular surface is completely detached from the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Identify the AO code for a spiral fracture of the humeral diaphysis.
back:
• Code: 12-A1.
• 1 (Humerus), 2 (Diaphysis), A (Simple), 1 (Spiral).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which pharmacological intervention is mandatory for severe AO Type III/Open fractures?
back:
• Immediate IV broad-spectrum antibiotics (e.g., co-amoxiclav).
• Administer within 1 hour of injury to prevent infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [One of the most important steps. A broad-spectrum antibiotic should be chosen covering Gram-positive, Gram-negative and, if there is severe con - tamination, anaerobic organisms.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the AO bone code for the Tibia and the Radius/Ulna?
back:
• Tibia: 4.
• Radius/Ulna: 2.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Interpret the clinical signifcance of an AO '32-C' fracture classification.
back:
• Location: Femoral (3) Diaphysis (2).
• Morphology: Complex/Segmental (C).
• Implication: High-energy injury with no contact between main fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Femur 3... 2 Diaphysis] Page 423 (Book Page): [C – After reduction no contact... (segmental)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does the AO Spine Classification evaluate stability differently than long bones?
back:
• Uses the mechanism of injury (e.g., Magerl).
• Assesses the three-column model (Anterior, Middle, Posterior).
• Unstable if ≥2 columns are injured.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 410 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability... If two or more columns of the spine are injured, it is considered unstable.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does AO classification dictate the choice between absolute and relative stability?
back:
• Absolute Stability (Compression): Required for AO articular types (B/C).
• Relative Stability (Splintage/Nailing): Utilized for AO simple or segmental diaphyseal types (A/C).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [Absolute stability... desirable in intra-articular fractures... Relative stability. Allows a little movement at the frac - ture site, optimising the environment for callus formation]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In AO classification of the Tibia, what does segment '4' denote?
back: • The Malleolar segment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4... 4 Malleolar segment]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the first and second digits signify in the AO fracture classification system?
back:
• First digit: The specific bone involved (e.g., 1 for humerus).
• Second digit: The bone segment (1-proximal metaphysis, 2-diaphysis, 3-distal metaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the primary basis for the AO classification of spinal injuries?
back:
• Mechanism of injury.
• Used specifically to assess spinal stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 410 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How do AO diaphyseal and metaphyseal fracture types 'A' differ in nature?
back:
• Diaphyseal A: Simple fractures with >95% contact after reduction.
• Metaphyseal A: Extra-articular fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%)... Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How is a simple spiral fracture of the humeral shaft coded in the AO system?
back:
• Code: 12-A1.
• Breakdown: 1 (Humerus), 2 (Diaphysis), A (Simple), 1 (Spiral).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the surgical requirement for AO Type B or C intra-articular fractures?
back:
• Anatomical reduction of the articular surface.
• Absolute stability to prevent callus inhibiting joint motion.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [AO type B and type C fractures are intra-articular and as such the principles of treating intra-articular fractures need to be respected; namely, anatomical reduction of the articular surface and rigid stabilisation to allow early joint movement]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define a diaphyseal Type C fracture according to the AO system.
back:
• Segmental or multifragmentary fracture.
• Characterized by no contact between the two main fragments after reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments (segmental)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which AO metaphyseal fracture type is defined as 'partial articular'?
back:
• Type B.
• Part of the joint surface remains in continuity with the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
coreConcept: Metaphyseal Type B vs C Distinction
front: Q: Contrast the articular continuity of AO Metaphyseal Type B and Type C fractures.
back:
• Type B (Partial): Part of the joint remains attached to the diaphysis.
• Type C (Complete): No part of the joint remains attached to the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis... C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Why is absolute stability mechanically required for AO intra-articular classifications?
back:
• Prevents secondary bone healing (callus) that inhibits joint movement.
• Optimizes the environment for direct (primary) bone healing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [This is desirable in intra-articular fractures, where callus at the fracture site might inhibit movement. Intra-articular fractures require an anatomical reduction and absolute stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What anatomic bone and segment are designated as '4' and '44'?
back:
• Bone 4: Tibia.
• Segment 44: Malleolar segment of the tibia/fibula.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4... 4 Malleolar segment]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the first and second numbers represent in an AO fracture classification code?
back:
• First number: Bone injured (e.g., 1=Humerus, 3=Femur).
• Second number: Bone segment (1=Proximal metaphysis, 2=Diaphysis, 3=Distal metaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The first number defines the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are AO diaphyseal fracture types A, B, and C differentiated?
back:
• A: Simple fracture (complete contact >90%).
• B: Wedge fracture (some contact between main fragments).
• C: Complex/Multifragmentary (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%); B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture); C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments (segmental).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO Metaphyseal types A, B, and C based on joint involvement.
back:
• Type A: Extra-articular (no joint involvement).
• Type B: Partial articular (part of joint attached to diaphysis).
• Type C: Complete articular (joint surface fully detached from diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular; B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis; C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the specific AO alphanumeric code for a spiral diaphyseal humeral fracture?
back:
12-A1. 
• 1: Humerus.
• 2: Diaphysis.
• A: Simple fracture.
• 1: Spiral pattern.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: According to AO principles, what treatment goal is required for intra-articular vs. extra-articular fractures?
back:
• Intra-articular: Anatomical reduction and absolute stability.
• Extra-articular: Mechanical alignment (length, rotation, axis) and relative stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [intra-articular fracture = anatomical reduction... extra-articular fracture = mechanical alignment. Focus on acceptable alignment, length and rotation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, which numbers identify the Humerus, Forearm, Femur, and Tibia?
back:
• 1: Humerus.
• 2: Radius/Ulna.
• 3: Femur.
• 4: Tibia/Fibula.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How is 'Absolute Stability' defined in AO principles regarding bone healing?
back:
• Definition: No movement/gap between fragments.
• Result: Direct (primary) bone healing without callus formation, utilizing osteoclastic cutting cones.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Absolute stability. Implies no displacement or movement and is achieved by accurate anatomical reduction with compression... Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does the AO system classify spinal injuries based on stability and risk?
back:
• Type A: Compression.
• Type B: Distraction.
• Type C: Rotation.
• Stability: Risk of neurological injury and instability increases from A to C.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [There are three main injury types, A, B and C, with increasing instability and risk of neurological injury. Type A fractures are vertebral body compression... Type B injuries involve distraction... type C injuries are rotational.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What defines 'Relative Stability' and its associated healing loop in the AO system?
back:
• Definition: Allows controlled movement (strain) at the fracture site.
• Result: Indirect (secondary) bone healing with callus formation transitioning from hematoma to bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Relative stability. Allows a little movement at the fracture site, optimising the environment for callus formation and indirect bone healing.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the specific AO segment number for malleolar fractures of the ankle?
back:
44. 
• 4: Tibia/Fibula bone group.
• 4: Malleolar segment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4... 4 Malleolar segment.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO fracture classification, which numerical codes are assigned to the four long bones?
back: 1: Humerus. 2: Radius/Ulna. 3: Femur. 4: Tibia/Fibula.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the numbers 1, 2, and 3 signify regarding long bone segments in AO coding?
back: 1: Proximal metaphysis. 2: Diaphysis. 3: Distal metaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis (1), diaphysis (2), distal metaphysis (3)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define the three diaphyseal fracture types (A, B, and C) in the AO system.
back: A: Simple (two fragments). B: Wedge (partial contact). C: Multifragmentary/Complex (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – Simple; B – Wedge; C – Multifragmentary]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A distal femur fracture that is entirely extra-articular is classified as which AO metaphyseal type?
back: Type A: Extra-articular.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In AO classification, what distinguishes a Type B from a Type C metaphyseal fracture?
back: Type B: Partial articular (joint part remains attached to diaphysis). Type C: Complete articular (joint surface detached from diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis. C – Complete articular; none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which specific number is added to the segment code for the malleolar region of the tibia?
back: Segment code 4.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [4 Malleolar segment]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: According to the AO system, what information does the final digit in a fracture code provide?
back: Specific nature or subtype of the injury (e.g., spiral, oblique, or transverse).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The letter and number that follows further defnes the nature of the injury.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A humeral fracture classified as 12-A1 specifically describes which injury pattern?
back: Humerus (1), Diaphysis (2), Simple pattern (A), Spiral nature (1).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example... 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: On which two criteria are the AO classifications for spinal injuries primarily based?
back: Mechanism of injury and assessment of spinal stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 410 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations... are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What defines a diaphyseal Type A fracture in terms of cortical contact after reduction?
back: Complete contact (at least 95%) between the two main fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: What do the first two digits in the AO fracture classification system represent?
back:
1. First digit: Bone involved (e.g., 1=humerus, 2=radius/ulna).
2. Second digit: Bone segment (1=proximal, 2=diaphysis, 3=distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The first number defines the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: In the AO diaphyseal classification, what distinguishes type A from type C?
back:
Type A: Simple fractures with complete contact between main fragments.
Type C: Complex/segmental fractures with no contact between main fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments... C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments (segmental).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Contrast AO metaphyseal Type B and Type C fractures based on articular involvement.
back:
Type B: Partial articular; joint remains partly attached to diaphysis.
Type C: Complete articular; joint surface is totally separated from diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis. C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: A radiograph shows a simple spiral mid-shaft humeral fracture. What is the AO code?
back: 12-A1. (1=Humerus, 2=Diaphysis, A=Simple pattern, 1=Spiral).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: How does the AO system categorize thoracic/thoracolumbar fractures based on instability?
back:
Type A: Compression (stable).
Type B: Distraction (less stable).
Type C: Rotational (highly unstable).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [There are three main injury types, A, B and C, with increasing instability... Type A fractures are vertebral body compression... Type B injuries involve distraction... type C injuries are rotational.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Which specific AO segment number identifies a malleolar ankle fracture?
back: Segment 4 (e.g., 44 represents bone 4 [tibia/fbula] and segment 4 [malleolar]).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [4 Malleolar segment]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Why is anatomical reduction mandatory for AO metaphyseal Type B and C fractures?
back: Because they are intra-articular. Precise reduction restores smooth joint movement and prevents secondary degenerative arthritis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [AO type B and type C fractures are intra-articular... anatomical reduction of the articular surface and rigid stabilisation to allow early joint movement and avoidance of degenerative joint disease.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Distinguish between AO extra-articular and complete articular fractures.
back:
Type A (Extra-articular): Fracture does not enter the joint surface.
Type C (Complete articular): Entire joint surface is fractured off the shaft.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [A – Extra-articular. C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: In the AO diaphyseal system, what characterizes Type B fractures?
back: Wedge fractures, where there is only partial contact between the main fragments after reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Which specific bone corresponds to the AO first digit '3'?
back: The Femur.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Femur 3]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the frst and second numbers represent in the AO fracture classifcation system?
back:
• First number: Bone involved (1=Humerus, 2=Forearm, 3=Femur, 4=Tibia).
• Second number: Bone segment (1=Proximal, 2=Diaphysis, 3=Distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are AO diaphyseal fracture types A, B, and C pathomorphologically distinguished?
back:
• Type A: Simple patterns (spiral/oblique/transverse).
• Type B: Wedge fractures.
• Type C: Multifragmentary or segmental fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types... A – Simple... B – Wedge... C – Multifragmentary/Segmental.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Distinguish AO metaphyseal fracture types A, B, and C based on joint involvement.
back:
• Type A: Extra-articular.
• Type B: Partial articular (part of joint remains attached to diaphysis).
• Type C: Complete articular (joint surface separated from diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types... A – Extra-articular... B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis... C – Complete articular; none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A patient has a spiral humeral shaft fracture. What is its exact AO alphanumeric code?
back: 12-A1. (1=Humerus, 2=Diaphysis, A=Simple, 1=Spiral).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, which specifc digits correspond to the femur and tibia respectively?
back:
• Femur: 3.
• Tibia: 4.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What defines an AO Type B diaphyseal fracture after reduction?
back: It is a wedge fracture characterized by partial contact between the two main fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are thoracic/thoracolumbar AO Type B and C injuries distinguished mechanistically?
back:
• Type B: Distraction of anterior or posterior elements.
• Type C: Rotational injuries (usually coexisting with A or B).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type B injuries involve distraction of the anterior or posterior elements and type C injuries are rotational and often coexist with type A or type B injuries.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: An intra-articular distal radial fracture shows no joint contact with the diaphysis. What is the AO type?
back: Type C (Complete articular). This requires anatomical reduction to prevent degenerative joint disease.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, how does Type A differ between diaphyseal and metaphyseal segments?
back:
• Diaphyseal Type A: Simple fracture pattern.
• Metaphyseal Type A: Extra-articular fracture (no joint surface involvement).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types... A – Simple... Metaphyseal types... A – Extra-articular.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the specifc AO classification used for subaxial spinal injuries?
back: The AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System (often used with the Magerl system).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the fundamental basis for the AO classification of fractures?
back:
A comprehensive alphanumeric system based on:
- Anatomical location (Bone and segment)
- Mechanism of injury
- Severity/Complexity
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.] Page 422 (Book Page): [The AO (Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Osteosynthesefragen) system provides a comprehensive classifcation of all fractures.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the frst four numbers in the AO bone coding system represent?
back:
1: Humerus
2: Radius and Ulna
3: Femur
4: Tibia
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, what are the three segment codes for long bones?
back:
1: Proximal metaphysis
2: Diaphysis
3: Distal metaphysis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [1 Proximal metaphysis, 2 Diaphysis, 3 Distal metaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How is a 12-A1 fracture decoded in the AO system?
back:
- 1: Humerus
- 2: Diaphysis
- A: Simple
- 1: Spiral
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO Diaphyseal types A, B, and C.
back:
A: Simple (one fracture line)
B: Wedge (partial contact between fragments)
C: Multifragmentary/Segmental (no contact between main fragments)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – simple... B – wedge... C – segmental]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define AO Metaphyseal types A, B, and C.
back:
A: Extra-articular
B: Partial articular (part of joint remains attached to diaphysis)
C: Complete articular (joint surface separated from diaphysis)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular... B – Partial articular... C – Complete articular]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which AO spine fracture type involves distraction of elements?
back: Type B injuries.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type B injuries involve distraction of the anterior or posterior elements]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What defines an AO Type C injury in the thoracic and thoracolumbar spine?
back: Rotational injuries, which often coexist with Type A (compression) or Type B (distraction) patterns.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type C injuries are rotational and often coexist with type A or type B injuries.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Describe AO Type A spine fractures in the thoracic region.
back: Vertebral body compression fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type A fractures are vertebral body compression fractures.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
coreConcept: Surgical Indications for Spinal AO Categories
front: Q: Which AO fracture category for thoracic spine typically requires surgical stabilization?
back: The majority of Type B (distraction) and Type C (rotational) injuries.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [The majority of type B and type C injuries require surgical stabilisation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the first two digits in an AO fracture classification code represent?
back:
- First Digit: Specific Bone (1-Humerus, 2-Radius/Ulna, 3-Femur, 4-Tibia/Fibula).
- Second Digit: Bone Segment (1-Proximal, 2-Diaphysis, 3-Distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: prox - imal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are diaphyseal fracture patterns categorized by letter in the AO system?
back:
- A: Simple fracture (complete contact >95%).
- B: Wedge fracture (contact remains between main fragments).
- C: Multifragmentary/Complex (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types ... A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%) ... B – wedge fracture ... C – segmental.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO 'Type B' fractures in diaphyseal versus metaphyseal locations.
back:
- Diaphyseal B: Wedge fracture pattern.
- Metaphyseal B: Partial articular fracture (joint remains partially attached to the diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal ... B – wedge fracture ... Metaphyseal ... B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Identify the specific AO code for a spiral fracture occurring in the humeral shaft.
back:
Code: 12-A1. 
- 1: Humerus.
- 2: Diaphysis.
- A: Simple pattern.
- 1: Spiral subtype.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which AO thoracic/thoracolumbar classification types usually indicate the need for surgical stabilization?
back:
- Type B (Distraction injuries).
- Type C (Rotational injuries).
- These exhibit significantly higher instability than Type A.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [The majority of type B and type C injuries require surgical stabilisation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define the hallmark of an AO 'Type C' metaphyseal fracture.
back:
- Complete articular fracture.
- No part of the joint surface remains attached to the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the primary basis for the AO spinal classification systems?
back:
- The mechanism of injury.
- Used specifically to assess spinal stability (e.g., Magerl or Subaxial systems).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Differentiate AO Thoracolumbar Type A from Type B based on injury pattern.
back:
- Type A: Vertebral body compression fractures.
- Type B: Distraction (tension failure) of anterior or posterior elements.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type A fractures are vertebral body compression fractures. Type B injuries involve distraction of the anterior or posterior elements.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, what specific bone is designated by the number 4?
back: - The Tibia and Fibula (Lower Leg).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4] (Figure 32.10)

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What does the segment number '4' represent in AO classification?
back: - The malleolar segment of the ankle.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [4 Malleolar segment] (Figure 32.10)

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, which numbers represent the humerus, femur, and tibia?
back:
1: Humerus
2: Radius and ulna
3: Femur
4: Tibia and fbula
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: For diaphyseal fractures, what do the letters A, B, and C signify?
back:
A: Simple (two fragments)
B: Wedge (three fragments)
C: Complex/Multifragmentary (no contact between main fragments)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%); B – partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture); C – no contact between the two main fragments (segmental)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How do AO metaphyseal types B and C differ regarding joint involvement?
back:
Type B: Partial articular (some joint remains attached to diaphysis)
Type C: Complete articular (joint surface fully detached from diaphysis)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis; C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A spiral fracture in the mid-shaft humerus is coded as what in AO?
back:
Code: 12-A1
(1: Humerus; 2: Diaphysis; A: Simple; 1: Spiral)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the clinical implication of an AO type C articular fracture?
back: Requires anatomical reduction and absolute stability to restore joint congruity and prevent secondary degenerative arthritis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [Intra-articular fractures: AO type B and type C fractures are intra-articular and as such the principles of treating intra-articular fractures need to be respected; namely, anatomical reduction of the articular surface and rigid stabilisation to allow early joint movement and avoidance of degenerative joint disease]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In AO classification, what do the segment numbers 1, 2, and 3 represent?
back:
1: Proximal metaphysis
2: Diaphysis
3: Distal metaphysis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [1 Proximal metaphysis, 2 Diaphysis, 3 Distal metaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which specific segment code is unique to the tibia and fibula region?
back: Segment code 4, representing the malleolar segment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4 ... 4 Malleolar segment]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO metaphyseal Type A with Types B/C regarding the joint.
back:
Type A: Extra-articular (joint not involved)
Types B/C: Intra-articular (articular surface involved)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular; B – Partial articular; C – Complete articular]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does AO type A1 diaphyseal morphology influence the healing goal?
back: A1 is a simple spiral pattern; the goal is mechanical restoration of length, alignment, and rotation via relative or absolute stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal fractures: Extra-articular fractures do not require an anatomical reduction, but rather a mechanical restoration by correction of length, alignment and rotation]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the defining characteristic of an AO type B diaphyseal fracture?
back: Wedge fracture: partial contact remains between the two main bone fragments after reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO fracture classification system, what do the first and second digits represent?
back:
1. First digit: Specific bone (e.g., 1=Humerus, 2=Radius/Ulna, 3=Femur, 4=Tibia/Fibula).
2. Second digit: Bone segment (1=Proximal metaphysis, 2=Diaphysis, 3=Distal metaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: prox - imal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does increasing the AO classification letter (A to C) reflect injury severity?
back: It indicates a progression from simple injury to higher energy, multifragmentary patterns with increased mechanical instability and poorer prognosis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [There are three main injury types, A, B and C, with increasing instability and risk of neurological injury.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast the definitions of AO Diaphyseal Type B and Type C fractures.
back:
1. Type B: Wedge fracture (some cortical contact remains between main fragments).
2. Type C: Complex/Segmental fracture (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – After reduction; partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture). C – After reduction; no contact between the two main fragments (segmental).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Apply the AO code for a simple spiral fracture occurring in the humeral shaft.
back: Code: 12-A1. (1 = Humerus, 2 = Diaphysis, A = Simple, 1 = Spiral).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Why is identification of AO Type C fractures critical regarding pharmacological prophylaxis?
back: Type C (multifragmentary/high-energy) fractures carry higher risks of soft tissue damage and open wounds, mandating immediate broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotic prophylaxis to prevent infection.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 444 (Book Page): [It has been shown that early administration of intravenous antibiotics is one of the most important steps. A broad-spectrum antibiotic should be chosen covering Gram-positive, Gram-negative and, if there is severe con - tamination, anaerobic organisms.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the primary defining feature of an AO Metaphyseal Type A fracture?
back: It is an extra-articular fracture; the fracture line does not extend into the joint surface.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [A – Extra-articular; complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How is the 'malleolar segment' of the tibia/fibula uniquely coded in AO?
back: The malleolar segment is designated with the bone-segment code '44'.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [4 Malleolar segment (under Tibia 4).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Distinguish between AO Metaphyseal Type B and Type C regarding articular involvement.
back:
1. Type B (Partial Articular): Part of the joint remains attached to the diaphysis.
2. Type C (Complete Articular): The entire joint surface is separated from the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis. C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
coreConcept: Fixation Principles Based on AO Type
front: Q: How does the AO classification guide the mechanical goal of fracture fixation?
back:
1. Simple/Articular (Type B/C): Usually requires absolute stability (compression) for direct healing.
2. Multifragmentary/Diaphyseal: Usually requires relative stability (splinting) for indirect healing (callus).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [Absolute stability... achieved by accurate anatomical reduction with compression... Relative stability... allows a little movement at the frac - ture site, optimising the environment for callus formation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: List the four AO bone numbers assigned to the major long bones.
back:
1: Humerus
2: Radius/Ulna
3: Femur
4: Tibia/Fibula
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
coreConcept: AO Numeric Bone and Segment Coding
front: Q: In the AO fracture classification system, what do the first two digits represent?
back:
1. First number: Specifies the bone injured (e.g., 1=humerus, 3=femur).
2. Second number: Defines the bone segment (1=proximal metaphysis, 2=diaphysis, 3=distal metaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The first number defines the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How do AO fracture types A, B, and C correlate with energy and clinical stability?
back:
Classification follows increasing energy transfer and instability:
* Type A: Simple/Extra-articular (most stable).
* Type B: Wedge/Partial articular.
* Type C: Multifragmentary/Complete articular (highest instability and risk of complications).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [There are three main injury types, A, B and C, with increasing instability and risk of neurological injury.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast the descriptive definitions of AO Type B and C for metaphyseal versus diaphyseal fractures.
back:
* Diaphyseal: B is a wedge fracture; C is segmental/multifragmentary.
* Metaphyseal: B involves partial articular surface contact; C involves complete articular separation from the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types... B – Wedge... C – Multifragmentary... Metaphyseal types... B – Partial articular... C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the full name of the AO system in fracture classification?
back: Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Osteosynthesefragen (Working Party on Problems of Bone Repair).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [AO, Arbeitsgemeinschaft für Osteosynthesefragen, may be translated from the German as ‘Working Party on Problems of Bone Repair’.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: On what primary basis are AO Spine classifications determined?
back: The mechanism of injury, used specifically to assess spinal stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO Type A definitions in diaphyseal versus metaphyseal fractures.
back:
● Diaphyseal A: Simple fracture (>95% contact).
● Metaphyseal A: Extra-articular fracture.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%). Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO code 12-A1, what do the first and second digits signify?
back:
● 1: The bone (Humerus).
● 2: The segment (Diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page)-423: [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured... For example, the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What does an AO Type B represent in a diaphyseal fracture?
back: A wedge fracture, characterized by partial contact between the main fragments after reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments (wedge fracture)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define AO Type C metaphyseal fractures.
back: Complete articular fractures where no part of the joint surface remains attached to the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: List the AO numeric codes for the four major long bones.
back:
● 1: Humerus
● 2: Radius and Ulna
● 3: Femur
● 4: Tibia
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1; Radius and ulna 2; Femur 3; Tibia 4]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Differentiate AO spinal fracture Types B and C.
back:
● Type B: Distraction of anterior/posterior elements.
● Type C: Rotational injuries (highest risk of neurological deficit).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Type B injuries involve distraction of the anterior or posterior elements and type C injuries are rotational and often coexist with type A or type B injuries.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are bone segments numbered (1, 2, 3) in the AO system?
back:
● 1: Proximal metaphysis
● 2: Diaphysis
● 3: Distal metaphysis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [1 Proximal metaphysis; 2 Diaphysis; 3 Distal metaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Define AO Type A spinal fractures.
back: Vertebral body compression fractures (least unstable AO spinal type).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [There are three main injury types, A, B and C, with increasing instability... Type A fractures are vertebral body compression fractures.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO fracture classification system, what do the first two numbers designate?
back:
1st number: Identifies the bone (e.g., 1=Humerus, 3=Femur).
2nd number: Identifies the segment (1=Proximal, 2=Diaphysis, 3=Distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The first number defines the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: proximal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are AO diaphyseal fractures categorized by the letters A, B, and C?
back:
A: Simple (two fragments).
B: Wedge (partial contact between main fragments).
C: Multifragmentary/Complex (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types: A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments; B – Wedge fracture; C – Multifragmentary/Complex.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Contrast AO Metaphyseal types A, B, and C regarding joint involvement.
back:
A: Extra-articular.
B: Partial articular (part of joint attached to diaphysis).
C: Complete articular (joint completely separated from diaphysis).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal types: A – Extra-articular; B – Partial articular; C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Assign the AO code for a simple spiral fracture of the humeral shaft.
back:
Code: 12-A1.
1: Humerus.
2: Diaphysis.
A: Simple.
1: Spiral.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the primary treatment goal for AO Type B and C metaphyseal fractures?
back: Anatomical reduction of the articular surface and absolute stability (rigid fixation) to allow early joint movement and prevent degenerative disease.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [AO type B and type C fractures are intra-articular and as such the principles of treating intra-articular fractures need to be respected; namely, anatomical reduction of the articular surface and rigid stabilisation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Which specific AO bone numbers represent the Humerus and the Tibia?
back:
Humerus: 1.
Tibia: 4.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1... Tibia 4.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In AO classification, what is unique about segment 4 of bone 4?
back: Segment 4 for bone 4 (Tibia) specifically represents the malleolar segment (ankle).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Tibia 4... 4 Malleolar segment.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Differentiate AO diaphyseal B and C based on post-reduction contact.
back:
Type B (Wedge): >95% contact or partial contact remains.
Type C (Multifragmentary): No contact between the two main fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – After reduction partial contact between the two main fragments... C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments (segmental).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Why is AO Type C considered the most severe diaphyseal fracture?
back: It is multifragmentary/segmental, has no fragment contact after reduction, and requires bridging fixation to provide relative stability for indirect healing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis... C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: Assign the bone numbers for the Radius/Ulna and Femur in the AO system.
back:
Radius/Ulna: 2.
Femur: 3.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Radius and ulna 2... Femur 3.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What do the first and second digits signify in the AO long bone fracture classification system?
back:
- First digit: Identifies the bone (e.g., 1=Humerus, 3=Femur).
- Second digit: Identifies the segment (1=Proximal, 2=Diaphysis, 3=Distal).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured: prox - imal metaphysis, diaphysis, distal metaphysis.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How are diaphyseal fractures categorized by morphology using AO letters A, B, and C?
back:
- A: Simple fractures (complete contact >95%).
- B: Wedge fractures (partial contact).
- C: Segmental or multifragmentary fractures (no contact between main fragments).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Diaphyseal types... A – After reduction complete contact between the two main fragments (>95%) B – After reduction partial contact... C – After reduction no contact between the two main fragments (segmental)]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What is the defining difference between AO metaphyseal Type B and Type C fractures?
back:
- Type B: Partial articular; some of the joint remains attached to the diaphysis.
- Type C: Complete articular; the joint is entirely detached from the diaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [B – Partial articular; some part of the joint remains in continuity with the diaphysis C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A radiograph shows a simple spiral fracture of the humeral diaphysis. What is the AO alphanumeric code?
back:
Code 12-A1:
- 1: Humerus
- 2: Diaphysis
- A: Simple morphology
- 1: Spiral pattern
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [the previously described humeral fracture would be 12-A1 (1 humerus, 2 diaphysis, A simple, 1 spiral).]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
coreConcept: Absolute Stability and Primary Bone Healing
front: Q: What management step is essential for AO Type C articular fractures to ensure direct bone healing?
back:
- Accurate anatomical reduction of the joint surface.
- Rigid stabilization to achieve 'Absolute Stability.'
- Compression across the fracture interface.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Intra-articular fractures require an anatomical reduction and absolute stability... It happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability with no movement or gap]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: What specific anatomical segment is designated by the number 4 in the AO classification of the tibia?
back:
- The malleolar segment.
- It is the only long bone with four segment classifications.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [4 Malleolar segment... The frst number defnes the bone injured and the second number the segment of bone injured]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: On what primary diagnostic factor are AO spinal classifications (like the Magerl system) based?
back:
- The mechanism of injury.
- Used specifically to assess spinal stability across the three columns.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 389 (Book Page): [The AO classifcations (Magerl and AO Spine Subaxial Classifcation System) are based on the mechanism of injury and are used to assess spinal stability.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: A patient presents with a multifragmentary femur fracture with complete joint detachment. Provide the AO class.
back:
Class 33-C:
- 3: Femur
- 3: Distal metaphysis
- C: Complete articular (complex/shattered).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Femur 3... 3 Distal metaphysis... C – Complete articular; an intra-articular fracture with none of the joint attached to the diaphysis]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: How does AO Type A diaphyseal morphology dictate the intended physiological healing loop?
back:
- High contact allows for 'Absolute Stability.'
- Promotes direct (primary) healing via osteoclastic cutting cones.
- Eliminates callus formation by minimizing fracture site movement (strain).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 423 (Book Page): [Absolute stability... is achieved by accurate anatomical reduction with compression... Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation.]

category: Explain the classification of fractures using the AO system
front: Q: In the AO system, which numbers represent the Humerus, Radius/Ulna, Femur, and Tibia?
back:
- 1: Humerus
- 2: Radius and Ulna
- 3: Femur
- 4: Tibia
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Humerus 1, Radius and ulna 2, Femur 3, Tibia 4]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What are the two primary requirements for direct (primary) bone healing?
back:
1. Absolute stability (no movement).
2. Anatomical cortical apposition (no gap).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability with no movement or gap between the fracture fragments.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Describe the sequence of tissue stages in indirect (secondary) bone healing.
back: Haematoma → Fibrous tissue → Soft callus → Hard callus (mineralisation) → Mature bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Indirect bone healing involves a transition from one tissue to another... from haematoma to fibrous tissue and then to soft callus, followed by mineralisation and formation of mature bone.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Contrast the role of stability in direct vs. indirect bone healing.
back:
1. Direct: Requires absolute stability (no callus).
2. Indirect: Requires relative stability (some movement/strain promotes callus).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation. It happens in an environment of... absolute stability... Indirect bone healing... is the most common form... a little movement is good.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: When is a fracture clinically and radiologically diagnosed as a non-union?
back: Fails to improve clinically or radiologically over 3 months, or shows no potential to heal (usually after 6 months).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [A non-union can also be defned as a fracture that fails to demonstrate clinical or radiological improvement over 3 months. In general, you do not describe a fracture as ‘non-union’ until 6 months after the injury.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Which specific class of analgesics is noted for slowing the bone healing process?
back: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 451 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include... non-steroidal anti-infammatory drugs]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What is the radiological defining feature of clinical fracture union?
back: Presence of callus bridging the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Radiologically a fracture has united when the callus bridges the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: According to Perren’s theory, what strain levels result in fibrous tissue vs. hard callus?
back:
1. Fibrous tissue: Under 100% strain.
2. Hard callus: Under 2% strain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [The amount of strain determines the nature of tissue it diferentiates into: under 100% leads to fbrous tissue... less than 2% hard callus]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Differentiate the primary causes of atrophic vs. hypertrophic non-union.
back:
1. Atrophic: Biological failure (poor blood supply/stimulus).
2. Hypertrophic: Mechanical failure (excessive movement at fracture site).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [In an atrophic non-union, the problem is generally a biological one... A hypertrophic non-union generally occurs when there is too much movement at the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What effect does Diabetes Mellitus have on the expected time to fracture union?
back: It approximately doubles the time required for union.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 451 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union)]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Define the 'consolidation' phase of fracture healing radiographically.
back: The stage following union marked by the return of the normal cortical bone pattern.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Consolidation: This follows union... Radiologically it is demonstrated by the return of the normal cortical pattern.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What are the two primary modes of bone healing following a fracture?
back:
1. Direct (primary) bone healing.
2. Indirect (secondary) bone healing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Following a fracture, bone can heal in two diferent ways: direct (primary) bone healing or indirect (secondary) bone healing.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What mechanical and biological environment is required for direct bone healing?
back:
1. Cortical apposition.
2. Absolute stability (zero movement).
3. Compression across fragments.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [It happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability with no movement or gap between the fracture fragments.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Distinguish the radiographic features of primary versus secondary bone healing.
back:
1. Direct (Primary): Heals directly without callus formation.
2. Indirect (Secondary): Heals through tissue differentiation and visible callus formation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation... Indirect bone healing involves a transition from one tissue to another with callus formation.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Why is absolute stability mandatory for intra-articular fracture healing?
back:
1. Allows anatomical restoration of the joint surface.
2. Prevents external callus, which would otherwise inhibit joint movement.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [This is desirable in intra-articular fractures, where callus at the fracture site might inhibit movement.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Which systemic metabolic condition is specifically known to double the expected time for union?
back: Diabetes mellitus; it impairs microscopic inflow and tissue perfusion at the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 451 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union)]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What clinical and radiological criteria define fracture 'union'?
back:
1. Clinical: Ability to withstand physiological loads with minimal pain/tenderness.
2. Radiological: Callus bridges the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [The fracture has healed sufciently from a clinical perspective to withstand physiological loads, with very little pain... united when the callus bridges the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: According to Perren’s theory, what strain level allows for soft callus formation?
back:
1. Fibrous tissue: <100% strain.
2. Soft callus: <10% strain.
3. Hard callus: <2% strain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [under 100% leads to fbrous tissue, under 10% soft callus, less than 2% hard callus and progressive mineralisation (Perren’s theory of bone healing).]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Distinguish atrophic from hypertrophic non-union based on their underlying pathology.
back:
1. Atrophic: Biological failure due to lack of blood supply or stimulus.
2. Hypertrophic: Mechanical failure due to excessive movement/instability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [In an atrophic non-union, the problem is generally a biological one... A hypertrophic non-union generally occurs when there is too much movement at the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Describe the cellular mechanism of direct bone remodeling via cutting cones.
back:
1. Osteoclasts form 'cutting cones' through the fracture interface.
2. Osteoblasts follow to deposit lamellar bone directly across the line.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Osteoclastic cutting cones cut across the fracture line, with following osteoblasts laying down lamellar bone across the fracture.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What is the chronological tissue differentiation sequence in indirect bone healing?
back:
1. Haematoma.
2. Fibrous tissue.
3. Soft callus.
4. Hard callus/Mineralisation.
5. Mature bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [the tissue undergoes diferentiation, from haematoma to fbrous tissue and then to soft callus, followed by mineralisation and formation of mature bone.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What are the two primary biological pathways for fracture healing?
back:
1. Direct (primary) bone healing
2. Indirect (secondary) bone healing
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Following a fracture, bone can heal in two different ways: direct (primary) bone healing or indirect (secondary) bone healing.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Describe the microscopic mechanism of direct (primary) bone healing.
back: Osteoclastic cutting cones traverse the fracture site, followed by osteoblasts depositing lamellar bone across the interface.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Osteoclastic cutting cones cut across the fracture line, with following osteoblasts laying down lamellar bone across the fracture.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Contrast the stability requirements for direct versus indirect bone healing.
back: Direct healing requires absolute stability (no movement/gap); indirect healing requires relative stability (controlled movement/strain).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page)-446: [Direct bone healing... happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability... Indirect bone healing... requires a varying strain.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: A fracture fails to unite and shows significant external callus. What is the likely pathology?
back: Hypertrophic non-union, typically caused by excessive movement or mechanical instability at the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [A hypertrophic non-union generally occurs when there is too much movement at the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Which common drug class slows bone healing according to systemic factors?
back: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 451 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include... non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What is the defining radiological feature of indirect bone healing absent in direct healing?
back: Callus formation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 445 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation. ... Indirect bone healing involves a transition from one tissue to another with callus formation.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: According to Perren’s theory, what strain level is required for hard callus formation?
back: A strain level of less than 2%.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [The amount of strain determines the nature of tissue... less than 2% hard callus and progressive mineralisation (Perren’s theory of bone healing).]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Differentiate the primary cause of atrophic versus hypertrophic non-union.
back: Atrophic non-union is due to biological failure (lack of blood supply); Hypertrophic non-union is due to mechanical failure (excessive movement).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [In an atrophic non-union, the problem is generally a biological one... A hypertrophic non-union generally occurs when there is too much movement.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Outline the tissue differentiation sequence in indirect bone healing.
back: Haematoma -> Fibrous tissue -> Soft callus -> Hard callus -> Mature bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [The tissue undergoes differentiation, from haematoma to fibrous tissue and then to soft callus, followed by mineralisation and formation of mature bone.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Define the radiological state of 'consolidation' in fracture management.
back: The return of the normal cortical bone pattern across the fracture site following union.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 446 (Book Page): [Consolidation: This follows union... Radiologically it is demonstrated by the return of the normal cortical pattern.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: What defines clinical and radiological fracture union?
back:
- Clinical: Ability to withstand physiological loads with minimal pain/tenderness.
- Radiological: Callus bridges the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [The fracture has healed suffciently from a clinical perspective to withstand physiological loads, with very little pain and minimal tenderness at the fracture site. Radiologically a fracture has united when the callus bridges the fracture site.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Contrast the requirements for direct vs. indirect bone healing.
back:
- Direct: Absolute stability (no movement) and cortical apposition; no callus.
- Indirect: Relative stability (some movement/strain) and callus formation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Direct (primary) bone healing... happens in an environment of cortical apposition and absolute stability with no movement or gap... Indirect (secondary) bone healing involves a transition from one tissue to another with callus formation.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
front: Q: Why is absolute stability mandatory for intra-articular fractures?
back:
- To ensure anatomical reduction.
- To promote direct bone healing without callus, which would otherwise inhibit joint movement.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 426 (Book Page): [Absolute stability... is desirable in intra-articular fractures, where callus at the fracture site might inhibit movement. Intra-articular fractures require an anatomical reduction and absolute stability.]

category: Describe principles of fracture healing
