front: Q: What secondary bone pathology leads to fragility fractures in spinal cord injury patients?
back: Disuse osteoporosis, which is an inevitable consequence of the injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.]

category: Define osteoporotic fractures and their clinical features
front: Q: What is the primary surgical goal when treating lower limb osteoporotic fractures in the elderly?
back: Fixation strong enough to allow immediate weight-bearing to facilitate early mobilization.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [fixation should be strong enough to allow immediate weight-bearing and to hold the position until union.]

category: Define osteoporotic fractures and their clinical features
front: Q: How does locking plate technology improve fixation in soft osteoporotic bone?
back: Screws thread into the plate to create a fixed-angle construct, increasing pull-out strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 431 (Book Page): [Locking plate technology improves fixation in osteoporotic bone, and bone void fllers can be utilised]

category: Define osteoporotic fractures and their clinical features
front: Q: When should primary arthroplasty be considered over fixation for osteoporotic periarticular fractures?
back: When stable fixation is impossible and early mobilization is essential to prevent complications.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [primary and revision arthroplasty have been considered in these situations to allow early mobilisation.]

category: Define osteoporotic fractures and their clinical features
front: Q: What specific complication is common when standard screws are used in osteoporotic metaphyseal bone?
back: Implants may "cut out" due to reduced pull-out strength in soft bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 431 (Book Page): [rigid fxation devices may cut out of soft bone, particularly in the metaphysis of the bone where pull-out strength of the fxation is reduced.]

category: Define osteoporotic fractures and their clinical features
front: Q: List two surgical adjuncts used to stabilize osteoporotic fractures with bone loss.
back: 1. Bone void fillers. 2. Injectable bone substitutes.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 432 (Book Page): [Injectable bone substitutes may be used to fll bone voids and augment fxation.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: List the four most common anatomical sites for osteoporotic fractures in the elderly.
back:
• Proximal femur (Hip)
• Thoracic and lumbar vertebrae (Spine)
• Distal radius (Wrist)
• Pelvis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture... Page 420 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group [Thoracic spine].

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Describe the characteristic mechanism of osteoporotic fractures in the thoracic spine.
back:
• Results in wedge compression fractures
• Caused by low-energy axial loading
• Vertebral body collapses due to significantly reduced bone mineral density
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Contrast the vascular risk between intracapsular and extracapsular hip fractures.
back:
• Intracapsular: High risk of avascular necrosis due to disrupted blood supply to the femoral head
• Extracapsular: Vascularity is typically preserved; risk is focused on mechanical stability
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): Fractures proximal to the hip capsule are intracapsular and those distal to the capsule are extracapsular fractures... A displaced intracapsular fracture may cause disruption of the blood supply... leading to avascular necrosis.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An 80-year-old presents with a shortened, externally rotated leg after a standing fall. What is the suspected site?
back:
• Proximal femur (Hip)
• Specifically suggestive of a displaced femoral neck fracture
• Common low-energy osteoporotic injury
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 417 (Book Page): A shortened externally rotated leg in an older patient suggests a fracture of the proximal femur.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which two surgical techniques are specifically utilized to augment osteoporotic metaphyseal fractures?
back:
• Injectable bone cement augmentation (e.g., vertebroplasty)
• Locking plate technology to prevent screw 'cut-out' from soft bone
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Treatment of lower limb osteoporotic fractures in older patients is challenging... may require specialised fxation techniques with locking screw/plate technology and injectable bone cement augmentation.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Define the energy threshold that characterizes a fracture as osteoporotic (fragility fracture).
back:
• Fracture resulting from 'low-energy' trauma
• Classically defined as a fall from standing height or less
• Indicates bone mineral density is insufficient for physiological loads
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why is locking plate fixation clinically superior for osteoporotic fractures compared to conventional plating?
back:
• Screws secure into the plate, creating a fixed-angle construct
• Relies on the plate-screw interface rather than bone-thread friction
• Significantly reduces risk of implant failure in porotic metaphyses
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 431 (Book Page): locking plates where the screw secures itself into the plate are design features to help improve cut-out strength and may help reduce failure of fxation in osteoporotic bone.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Distinguish a typical osteoporotic hip fracture from a pathological fracture by history.
back:
• Osteoporotic: History of low-energy mechanical fall
• Pathological: Minimal/no trauma; history of constitutional symptoms or malignancy; inconsistent with injury severity
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): A pathological fracture should be suspected if the history is not consistent with the severity of the injury. The patient may give a history of low-energy injury that normally would not cause a fracture.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Describe the metabolic loop leading to fragility at common osteoporotic sites.
back:
• Reduced bone mineral density -> 
• Compromised micro-architecture -> 
• Structural failure under normal load or minor trauma
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which specific wrist fracture pattern is most common in osteoporotic falls?
back:
• Colles' fracture
• Distal radius fracture with dorsal displacement/angulation
• Often occurring after a fall on an outstretched hand
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): Most dorsally displaced fractures (Colles fracture) can be addressed with closed reduction and held in a cast.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What is the most common anatomical site for osteoporotic fractures in the vertebral column?
back: Thoracic spine (specifically T1–T10).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Thoracic spine (T1–T10). Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Describe the specific mechanical failure pattern seen in osteoporotic vertebral fractures.
back: Wedge compression fracture caused by the collapse of cancellous bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Compression fractures occur when cancellous bone collapses; for example, vertebral wedge compression fracture.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: In the proximal femur, which two categories of sites are most vulnerable to osteoporotic fractures?
back:
1. Intracapsular (femoral neck)
2. Extracapsular (trochanteric).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): [Fractures proximal to the hip capsule are intracapsular and those distal to the capsule are extracapsular fractures... Intracapsular femoral neck fractures... are generally stable and interruption of the blood supply to the femoral head is rare.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An elderly patient suffers a fragility fracture at the wrist. Identify the most likely anatomical site.
back: Distal radius (classically presenting as a Colles’ fracture).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): [Most dorsally displaced fractures (Colles fracture) can be addressed with closed reduction and held in a cast... in the distal radius.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which site in the proximal upper limb is frequently affected by periarticular osteoporotic fractures?
back: Proximal humerus.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): [reverse polarity shoulder arthroplasty are current treatment options for older patients with osteoporotic periarticular fractures... In fractures of the proximal humerus.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Identify a common osteoporotic fracture site in the distal lower limb of older patients.
back: Metaphysis of the distal femur.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures of the distal femur are amenable to internal fxation with locked intramedullary nails or plate and screw fxation.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why are metaphyseal regions more susceptible to osteoporotic fractures than diaphyseal regions?
back: They contain high volumes of cancellous bone, which collapses more readily when bone mineral density is reduced.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Compression fractures occur when cancellous bone collapses] and Page 437 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures... are amenable to internal fxation.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: A minor fall resulting in a fracture at a common osteoporotic site is termed what?
back: Low-energy fragility fracture.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Identify the most frequent osteoporotic fracture site in the pelvis of older adults.
back: Pubic rami (Stable Type A fractures).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 384 (Book Page): [Type A... result from lateral compression, which causes compression fractures of the pubic rami... [common in] older adults.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: List the four major anatomical regions targeted in osteoporotic fracture screening.
back:
1. Spine (Vertebrae)
2. Hip (Proximal femur)
3. Wrist (Distal radius)
4. Shoulder (Proximal humerus).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Synthesized from Page 421 (Book Page): [Thoracic spine], Page 434 (Book Page): [Distal radius], Page 436 (Book Page): [Proximal humerus], and Page 437 (Book Page): [Proximal femur].

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: List the three most common anatomical sites for osteoporotic fractures in elderly patients.
back:
1. Proximal femur (Hip)
2. Distal radius (Wrist)
3. Thoracic and lumbar vertebrae (Spine)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): [An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture, multiple rib fractures...] Page 413 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group (thoracic spine).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Describe the typical presentation of an osteoporotic fracture involving the thoracic spine.
back: It presents as a wedge compression fracture, where the anterior part of the vertebral body collapses under minimal stress.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 419 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group (Thoracic spine (T1–T10)).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Which distal radius fracture pattern is most frequently caused by a fall on an outstretched hand in elderly patients?
back: Colles fracture, characterized by dorsal displacement and angulation of the distal fragment ('dinner fork' deformity).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): [Most dorsally displaced fractures (Colles fracture) can be addressed with closed reduction and held in a cast.] Page 480 (Book Page): [Look for bony deformity (dinner fork deformity, Colles’ fracture).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: An elderly patient presents with a shortened, externally rotated leg after a minor fall. What is the suspected injury?
back: A fracture of the proximal femur (hip fracture), typically either intracapsular or extracapsular.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 418 (Book Page): [A shortened externally rotated leg in an older patient suggests a fracture of the proximal femur.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: What drug class is primary for managing bone density and reducing fracture frequency in osteoporosis?
back: Bisphosphonates (e.g., Alendronate) are used to decrease bone resorption and turnover to enhance strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Define the relationship between 'low-energy injury' and osteoporotic bone failure.
back: Osteoporotic bone is characterized by low mineral density, making it liable to fracture during physiological loads, such as a fall from standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterized by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: How are proximal femoral fractures anatomically categorized relative to the joint capsule?
back:
1. Intracapsular: Proximal to the capsule attachment.
2. Extracapsular: Distal to the capsule attachment.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): [Fractures proximal to the hip capsule are intracapsular and those distal to the capsule are extracapsular fractures.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Contrast 'Real' versus 'Apparent' leg length discrepancy in the context of hip fractures or deformity.
back:
1. Real: Actual bone shortening (ASIS to medial malleolus).
2. Apparent: Pelvic tilt or fixed adduction making leg look short (Midline to medial malleolus).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 489 (Book Page): [The first is called ‘real’ LLD, measured ASIS to medial malleolus. The second is called ‘apparent’ LLD, measured midline, e.g. xiphisternum to medial malleolus.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Explain why surgical fixation with standard screws often fails in osteoporotic metaphyseal fractures.
back: Standard screws have reduced 'pull-out' strength in low-density cancellous bone, leading to screws 'cutting out' of the soft metaphysis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 431 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic intra-articular fractures are a considerable challenge... rigid fxation devices may cut out of soft bone, particularly in the metaphysis of the bone where pull-out strength of the fxation is reduced.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: What defines a 'pathological fracture' in clinical orthopaedics?
back: A fracture occurring through bone that has been weakened by an underlying disease process (e.g., osteoporosis, tumor) under normal mechanical loads.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [When abnormal bone fails under normal load this is referred to as a pathological fracture. The bone may be weakened by a primary bone tumour... osteoporosis.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What is the primary anatomical distinction between a complete and an incomplete fracture?
back:
- Complete: Fracture line spans the entire width of the bone (both cortices fail).
- Incomplete: Only one cortex fails; the other remains intact.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [In children and adolescents the fracture line may be incomplete... These incomplete fractures are called greenstick fractures... Adult transverse fracture failure across the whole bone.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What mechanical property of pediatric bone allows for the occurrence of incomplete fractures?
back:
- Plasticity: Pediatric bones are more plastic and less brittle than adult bones.
- Resistance: Allows the bone to bend or buckle rather than snap completely.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [In children and adolescents the fracture line may be incomplete because of the plastic, less brittle nature of their bones.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Differentiate the mechanics of a Greenstick fracture from a Torus (Buckle) fracture.
back:
- Greenstick: The bone fails on the tension side.
- Torus: The bone fails (buckles) on the compression side.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [These incomplete fractures are called greenstick fractures, where one tension cortex fails. If the compression cortex buckles, they are called torus or buckle fractures.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Clinical Scenario: A child presents with a bowed limb after a fall, but X-rays show no fracture line. Diagnosis?
back: - Plastic deformation: The bone has bent permanently without a visible cortical break due to pediatric elasticity.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Paediatric bone may also simply undergo plastic deformation without a visible fracture line.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Which pharmacological agent is used to reduce the frequency of incomplete/complete fractures in Osteogenesis Imperfecta?
back: - Cyclical bisphosphonates: These decrease bone resorption and turnover, increasing bone strength and reducing pain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What radiological criteria define an adult complete transverse fracture?
back:
- A fracture line traversing the full diameter of the diaphysis.
- Discontinuity of both the medial and lateral cortices.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Adult transverse fracture failure across the whole bone.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Why is the periosteal hinge more significant in reducing incomplete pediatric fractures than complete adult fractures?
back: - Stability: The thick, strong pediatric periosteum remains partially intact in incomplete fractures, guiding fragment alignment and holding the reduction.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 440 (Book Page): [The paediatric periosteum is often thick and very strong... The periosteal hinge should be preserved as it also allows for better holding of the fracture if it remains intact.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Differential Case: Which specific incomplete fracture pattern is pathognomonic for non-accidental injury (NAI)?
back: - Metaphyseal corner or bucket-handle fractures (avulsion-type incomplete fractures at the growth plate).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 637 (Book Page): [Characteristic patterns should alert the clinician to the possibility of non-accidental injury (NAI)... Corner or bucket-handle metaphyseal fractures.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: How does the type of bone healing typically differ between complete fractures treated with absolute vs. relative stability?
back:
- Absolute (Compression): Direct (Primary) bone healing with no callus.
- Relative (Movement): Indirect (Secondary) bone healing with callus formation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Direct bone healing... heals directly with bone and without callus formation... Indirect bone healing involves a transition from one tissue to another with callus formation.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Anatomical Fact: In a Greenstick fracture, which cortex remains intact to prevent a complete fracture?
back: - The compression cortex remains intact (while the tension cortex fails).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [These incomplete fractures are called greenstick fractures, where one tension cortex fails.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What is the most common site for osteoporotic fractures in the spinal column?
back:
- Thoracic spine (T1–T10).
- Typically presents as wedge compression fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group (Thoracic spine T1–T10).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Describe the biomechanical mechanism that characterizes an osteoporotic fracture.
back:
- Bone failure occurring under normal load.
- Low-energy mechanisms, such as a fall from standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Differentiate the primary management goal for intra-articular versus extra-articular osteoporotic fractures.
back:
- Intra-articular: Anatomical reduction of the joint surface.
- Extra-articular: Mechanical restoration (length, alignment, and rotation).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): [intra-articular fracture = anatomical reduction ... extra-articular fracture = mechanical alignment.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An 80-year-old falls from a chair. Which three sites must be prioritized for osteoporotic fracture assessment?
back:
1. Thoracic/Lumbar spine.
2. Proximal femur (hip).
3. Distal radius (wrist).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Treatment of lower limb osteoporotic fractures in older patients is challenging... Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which intervention specifically addresses painful, symptomatic osteoporotic wedge compression fractures?
back:
- Percutaneous bone cement augmentation.
- Known as vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults... symptomatic fractures can be treated with percutaneous bone cement augmentation, known as vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What constitutes the clinical diagnosis of a 'fragility fracture'?
back:
- Fracture resulting from low-energy trauma.
- Force equivalent to a fall from standing height or less.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why is internal fixation of the distal femur metaphysis particularly difficult in osteoporotic patients?
back:
- Reduced pull-out strength of screws.
- High risk of implants 'cutting out' of soft metaphyseal bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 432 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic intra-articular fractures are a considerable challenge... particularly in the metaphysis of the bone where pull-out strength of the fxation is reduced.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Differentiate 'pathological' from 'osteoporotic' fractures based on load characteristics.
back:
- Pathological: Bone fails under normal load due to underlying disease (tumour, infection).
- Osteoporotic: Bone fails due to low mineral density/strength, often during low-energy falls.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [When abnormal bone fails under normal load this is referred to as a pathological fracture... Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
coreConcept: Load-Bearing vs. Load-Sharing in Fragile Bone
front: Q: How does osteoporotic bone loss affect the surgical 'Load' principle?
back:
- Requires 'load-bearing' implants rather than 'load-sharing'.
- Ensures stability when the host bone cannot support physiological stress.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Depending on the cause of the pathological fracture the bone may not heal and consideration should be given to a load-bearing device not load-sharing.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: List common non-spinal sites specifically named in the text as prone to osteoporotic fractures.
back:
1. Proximal Humerus.
2. Distal Femur.
3. Proximal Femur.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Treatment of lower limb osteoporotic fractures... distal femur... proximal humerus.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What is the defining anatomical difference between a complete and an incomplete fracture?
back: A complete fracture involves failure across the entire bone. An incomplete fracture line does not traverse the whole bone, leaving part of the cortex intact.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [In children and adolescents the fracture line may be incomplete... These incomplete fractures are called greenstick fractures, where one tension cortex fails... adult transverse fracture failure across the whole bone]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What specific cortical failure occurs during a Greenstick fracture?
back: In a Greenstick fracture, the bone fails specifically on the tension side, while the opposite cortex remains functionally intact.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [greenstick fracture; the bone has failed on the tension side]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Contrast the cortical presentation of a Greenstick fracture versus a Torus fracture.
back:
● Greenstick: Tension cortex fails (fractures).
● Torus: Compression cortex buckles (bulges).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [greenstick fracture; the bone has failed on the tension side; torus or buckle fracture; the bone has failed on the compression side]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: A 6-year-old presents with wrist pain; X-ray shows a focal cortical bulge without a visible fracture line. Diagnosis?
back: Torus (Buckle) fracture. This is a common incomplete pediatric injury where the bone buckles under compression.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [If the compression cortex buckles, they are called torus or buckle fractures.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Why are incomplete fractures highly characteristic of the pediatric population compared to adults?
back: Paediatric bones are significantly more plastic and less brittle than adult bones, allowing them to deform without failing across the entire diameter.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [In children and adolescents the fracture line may be incomplete because of the plastic, less brittle nature of their bones.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: What are the three primary categories of incomplete bone injuries in children?
back:
1. Greenstick fractures
2. Torus (Buckle) fractures
3. Plastic deformation
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [These incomplete fractures are called greenstick fractures... torus or buckle fractures. Paediatric bone may also simply undergo plastic deformation without a visible fracture line.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: How is plastic deformation distinguished from other incomplete fractures on radiography?
back: It presents as a change in the overall shape or curvature of the bone without any visible cortical fracture line.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Paediatric bone may also simply undergo plastic deformation without a visible fracture line.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: Differentiate a complete transverse fracture from a Greenstick fracture in a forensic bone analysis.
back:
● Complete transverse: The fracture line passes through 100% of the bone diameter.
● Greenstick: The fracture line is partial, appearing only on the convex (tension) surface.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [adult transverse fracture failure across the whole bone; greenstick fracture; the bone has failed on the tension side]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: How does a Buckle fracture relate to the architectural 'Torus' concept?
back: The term is derived from the architectural 'torus' (column bulge), reflecting the localized swelling or 'buckling' of the compression cortex.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [Torus fractures take their name from an architectural torus, which is the ‘bulge’ at the base of a column.]

category: Differentiate between complete and incomplete fractures
front: Q: In an adult patient, is a spiral fracture of the humerus typically complete or incomplete?
back: Typically complete. In adults, fractures generally involve failure across the whole bone due to increased brittleness compared to children.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): [adult transverse fracture failure across the whole bone]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Identify the commonest osteoporotic fracture type occurring in the thoracic spine.
back: Wedge compression fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why is the bone metaphysis a high-risk site for osteoporotic fixation failure?
back:
1. Soft bone quality.
2. Reduced pull-out strength for rigid fixation devices.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 432 (Book Page): particularly in the metaphysis of the bone where pull-out strength of the fixation is reduced.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
coreConcept: Anatomic Distribution of Spinal Fragility Fractures
front: Q: Which specific thoracic levels are most susceptible to osteoporotic wedge compression?
back: T1–T10 (the thoracic spine).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): Thoracic spine (T1–T10) Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An older adult falling a few steps likely sustains which two types of fractures?
back:
1. Hip fracture.
2. Multiple rib fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture, multiple rib fractures...

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which lower limb metaphyseal site commonly requires specialized locking plates for osteoporotic fractures?
back: The distal femur.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): Metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures of the distal femur are amenable to internal fixation... Locking plate technology improves fixation in osteoporotic bone.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What clinical mechanism defines a typical osteoporotic fragility fracture?
back: Low-energy injuries, such as a fall from standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which extremity site has an significantly elevated infection risk during osteoporotic fracture fixation?
back: The ankle.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): ankle fracture fixation in the elderly also have high infection rates.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
coreConcept: Clinical Suspicion of Weak Bone Sites
front: Q: How is the suspected site of weak bone identified when a mechanism of injury seems minor?
back: Force mismatch: sustaining a fracture from a low-energy injury (osteoporotic or pathological bone).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): A pathological fracture should be suspected if the history is not consistent with the severity of the injury. The patient may give a history of low-energy injury that normally would not cause a fracture.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: How does osteoporosis pathologically affect the thoracic vertebrae?
back: Bone loss causes the vertebral bodies to collapse into a wedged posture.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which site commonly sustains osteoporotic fractures adjacent to a total knee replacement?
back: The distal femur (periprosthetic fractures).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): More commonly now these injuries are often next to a knee replacement (periprosthetic fracture)...

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which anatomical location is the most common site of osteoporotic fractures?
back: The thoracic spine (specifically T1–T10), typically presenting as wedge compression fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group [Thoracic spine (T1–T10)].]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why are metaphyseal bone regions specifically prone to osteoporotic fractures?
back: These areas contain high volumes of cancellous bone, which undergoes more rapid mineral loss and strength reduction than cortical bone.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 432 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic intra-articular fractures are a considerable challenge... because pull-out strength of the fxation is reduced... particularly in the metaphysis.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Contrast the stability of Colles’ versus Smith’s fractures in osteoporotic bone.
back: Colles’ (dorsal displacement) is the most common osteoporotic wrist fracture; Smith’s (volar) is inherently less stable and usually requires plate fixation.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): [Most volar displaced extra-articular distal radial fractures (Smith’s)... tend to be unstable and displace if held in a cast.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An elderly patient presents with a shortened, externally rotated leg after a minor fall. Identify the likely site.
back: Proximal femur (Neck of femur/Hip).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 418 (Book Page): [shortened externally rotated leg in an older patient suggests a fracture of the proximal femur.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What constitutes the hallmark "low-energy injury" leading to osteoporotic fractures?
back: A simple fall from a standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What clinical deformity characterizes an osteoporotic distal radius fracture?
back: "Dinner fork" deformity (characteristic of a Colles’ fracture).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 419 (Book Page): [Look for any bony deformity (dinner fork deformity, Colles’ fracture).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: How does osteoporosis influence the surgical management choice for proximal humerus fractures?
back: Low bone density often necessitates locking plate technology or primary reverse polarity shoulder arthroplasty to ensure fixation stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): [In [older patients with] osteoporosis... reverse polarity shoulder prosthesis... or plate fxation [with] locking plates [may be used].]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which fracture site is often associated with periprosthetic injury in osteoporotic bone?
back: The distal femur, typically occurring adjacent to a pre-existing knee replacement.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): [Metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures of the distal femur... are often next to a knee replacement (periprosthetic fracture).]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Describe the mechanical loop leading to "wedge compression" in the osteoporotic spine.
back: Anterior vertebral body collapse occurs under normal load because cancellous bone can no longer resist compressive forces.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Besides the spine and hip, name two other common metaphyseal sites for osteoporotic fractures.
back:
1. Distal radius (Wrist).
2. Proximal humerus (Shoulder).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): [dorsally displaced fractures (Colles fracture)... in the presence of osteoporosis]; Page 436 (Book Page): [In [older patients with] osteoporosis... reverse polarity shoulder prosthesis.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Define osteoporosis based on its skeletal characteristics and fracture risk.
back:
* Low bone mineral density (BMD).
* Reduced bone strength.
* Increased liability to fracture from low-energy injuries (fragility).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Describe the "disuse" mechanism of osteoporosis mentioned in clinical paralysis scenarios.
back:
* Inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury.
* Caused by lack of mechanical loading.
* Results in high risk of fragility fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 499 (Book Page): [Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Contrast the injury mechanisms of healthy versus osteoporotic bone failure.
back:
* Healthy bone: Requires extreme force (e.g., high-speed collision).
* Osteoporotic bone: Fails under minimal stress (e.g., fall from standing height).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: An older patient falls down a few steps and appears well. Why is this high-risk?
back:
* High risk for occult osteoporotic fragility fractures (hip/ribs).
* Mortality potentially exceeds younger patients with open long bone fractures.
* High likelihood of subdural haemorrhage.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): [An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture... At frst glance the patient can appear well, but their injury severity score (ISS) and potential mortality could easily exceed those of a younger patient with multiple open long bone fractures.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which drug class is used to inhibit bone resorption and strengthen pediatric metabolic bone?
back:
* Cyclical bisphosphonates.
* Decreases bone turnover.
* Reduces fracture rates and bone pain.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: List the components of the "female athlete triad" associated with osteoporosis risk.
back:
1. Disordered eating.
2. Amenorrhoea.
3. Osteoporosis.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How does repetitive training in female dancers specifically impact bone mineral health?
back:
* High incidence of stress fractures.
* Secondary to the female athlete triad (osteoporosis/amenorrhoea).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [Stress fractures are also found in female dancers as a result of repetitive training and can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: List three secondary metabolic conditions that increase the risk of pediatric physeal slips.
back:
1. Hypothyroidism.
2. Renal failure.
3. Previous radiotherapy (e.g., to pituitary).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 621 (Book Page): [Other conditions such as hypothyroidism, renal failure and previous radiotherapy (local or to the pituitary) also increase the risk.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Explain the physiological law that explains why inactivity leads to osteoporosis.
back:
* Wolff’s Law.
* Bone deposition and resorption depend on applied physical stresses.
* Reduced stress leads to resorption.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 609 (Book Page): [Wolff’s law: Bone deposition and resorption depend on the stresses applied.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Identify four systemic/lifestyle factors that double the time to fracture union.
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus.
2. Smoking.
3. Corticosteroid use.
4. Peripheral vascular disease.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 424 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union), diminished blood supply (peripheral vascular disease...)... smoking, non-steroidal anti-infammatory drugs.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What are the two primary defining characteristics of osteoporosis?
back:
- Low bone mineral density.
- Reduced bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Why is spinal cord injury a significant risk factor for osteoporosis?
back: It leads to disuse osteoporosis, making fragility fractures an inevitable consequence of the injury.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 404 (Book Page): [Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What are the three components of the female athlete triad risk group?
back:
- Osteoporosis.
- Disordered eating.
- Amenorrhoea.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea)]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What clinical scenario in an older adult classically indicates underlying osteoporosis?
back: A fragility fracture occurring from a low-energy injury, such as a fall from standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which two pharmacological classes are identified as high-risk for secondary bone loss?
back:
- Corticosteroids (Steroids).
- Immunosuppressant therapy.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 493 (Book Page): [Ask about all medication and the following in particular: anticoagulants, steroids, aspirin, immunosuppressant therapy]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which metabolic disease doubles the time to union and compromises bone health?
back: Diabetes mellitus.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 618 (Book Page): [well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union)]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How does Wolff’s Law explain bone loss in immobilized or sedentary patients?
back: Bone resorption occurs when the mechanical stresses required for deposition are absent.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 609 (Book Page): [Wolff’s law: Bone deposition and resorption depend on the stresses applied]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Why must smoking status be assessed as a risk factor for bone recovery?
back: Smoking is an essential risk factor that significantly slows bone healing and union.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 618 (Book Page): [Attention to... smoking cessation is essential. ...well-known factors that slow down bone healing include... smoking]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which nutritional deficiencies are the primary risk factors for inadequate bone mineralization?
back: Inadequate intake of Vitamin D and Calcium.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page): [Common causes of rickets: Nutritional: Reduced intake of vitamin D and calcium]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Why is advanced age considered a primary risk factor for osteoporotic limb trauma?
back: Older patients frequently have lower bone density, making low-energy fractures more technically challenging to fix.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Treatment of lower limb osteoporotic fractures in older patients is challenging.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which demographic is most susceptible to osteoporotic wedge compression fractures?
back: Older adults (commonest injury in this group).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How does a spinal cord injury pathophysiologically lead to osteoporosis?
back: Via disuse; it is an inevitable consequence resulting in fragility fractures due to lack of mechanical loading.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 404 (Book Page): [Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Contrast the components of the 'female athlete triad' associated with osteoporosis.
back:
1. Osteoporosis (low bone density)
2. Disordered eating (nutritional deficit)
3. Amenorrhoea (hormonal dysfunction).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea)]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: A 17-year-old female dancer has a metatarsal stress fracture and amenorrhoea. What is the suspected systemic risk factor?
back: Osteoporosis, as part of the female athlete triad commonly seen in high-intensity training.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [Stress fractures are also found in female dancers as a result of repetitive training and can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which pharmacological agent is used to improve bone strength and reduce fracture rates in pediatric brittle bone disease?
back: Cyclical bisphosphonates (they decrease bone resorption and turnover).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What is the defining clinical characteristic of osteoporotic bone failure in extremity trauma?
back: Liability to fracture with low-energy injuries, such as a fall from a standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Apply Wolff’s Law to explain the development of osteoporosis in immobilized patients.
back: Bone deposition/resorption depends on applied stress; lack of stress leads to increased resorption and decreased density (disuse).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 409 (Book Page): [Wolff’s law: Bone deposition and resorption depend on the stresses applied.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Differentiate the primary skeletal defect in Osteoporosis versus Rickets.
back: Osteoporosis involves low bone mass/density; Rickets involves inadequate mineralization of the growing bone matrix.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page): [In rickets, the primary problem is inadequate mineralisation of growing bone.] Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Describe the metabolic loop where renal disease acts as a risk factor for bone density loss.
back: Renal failure leads to secondary hyperparathyroidism, resulting in inadequate mineralization and bone weakening.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page): [Renal disease: End-stage renal failure, renal tubular anomalies. Secondary hyperparathyroidism may be present.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Name the two pathological parameters used to define osteoporosis in MSK medicine.
back:
1. Low bone mineral density
2. Reduced bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.]

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which anatomical region of the spine is most commonly affected by osteoporotic wedge compression fractures?
back:
- Thoracic spine
- Specifically segments T1–T10
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group. ... Thoracic spine (T1–T10)

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What is the classic clinical presentation of an osteoporotic proximal femoral (hip) fracture?
back:
- Shortened limb
- Externally rotated posture
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 417 (Book Page): A shortened externally rotated leg in an older patient suggests a fracture of the proximal femur.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Identify the most common osteoporotic fracture site in the wrist following a fall on an outstretched hand (FOOSH).
back:
- Distal radius (Colles fracture)
- Characterized by dorsal displacement
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 434 (Book Page): Most dorsally displaced fractures (Colles fracture) can be addressed with closed reduction and held in a cast. ... Distal radial fractures are very common.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Beyond the spine, hip, and wrist, which upper extremity site is frequently associated with osteoporotic fragility fractures?
back:
- Proximal humerus
- Often involving the anatomical neck or tuberosities
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): In fractures of the proximal humerus ... with osteoporosis and other comorbidities, consideration may be given to replacing the humeral head.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: How is an osteoporotic 'fragility fracture' defined in terms of mechanism of injury?
back:
- Failure of abnormal bone under normal load
- Typically a low-energy injury (e.g., fall from standing height)
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height). ... When abnormal bone fails under normal load this is referred to as a pathological fracture.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which specific hip fracture site carries the highest risk of avascular necrosis (AVN) in osteoporotic patients?
back:
- Displaced intracapsular femoral neck fractures
- Due to interruption of the blood supply via the hip capsule
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 436 (Book Page): A displaced intracapsular fracture may cause disruption of the blood supply ... leading to avascular necrosis.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What clinical finding differentiates an unstable osteoporotic ankle fracture from a stable one?
back:
- Involvement of multiple columns (medial, lateral, or posterior)
- Evidence of talar shift on imaging
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 438 (Book Page): If both or all three columns are involved or there is evidence of talar shift, it is an unstable injury.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An 80-year-old falls down two steps and presents with low back pain. Which concurrent injuries are most likely?
back:
- Hip fracture
- Multiple rib fractures
- Subdural haemorrhage
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture, multiple rib fractures and a small subdural haemorrhage.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why is internal fixation challenging in metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures?
back:
- Reduced screw 'pull-out' strength in soft cancellous bone
- Risk of fixation 'cutting out' of the bone
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 431 (Book Page): Osteoporotic intra-articular fractures are a considerable challenge. ... rigid fixation devices may cut out of soft bone, particularly in the metaphysis of the bone where pull-out strength ... is reduced.

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Which radiological feature defines a 'Torus' or 'Buckle' fracture often seen in weakened cortices?
back:
- Failure of the compression cortex
- Characterized by an outward bulging or buckling
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 422 (Book Page): If the compression cortex buckles, they are called torus ... or buckle fractures. ... the bone has failed on the compression side.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Define osteoporosis based on its two primary anatomical characteristics.
back:
1. Low bone mineral density.
2. Reduced bone strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Describe the physiological mechanism leading to osteoporosis after a spinal cord injury.
back: Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury, which significantly increases the risk of fragility fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 425 (Book Page): [Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Contrast the injury mechanisms of normal bone versus osteoporotic bone.
back: Normal bone requires significant force; osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture from low-energy injuries, such as a fall from standing height.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: A 20-year-old female athlete presents with stress fractures. Identify two metabolic risk factors.
back:
1. Disordered eating.
2. Amenorrhoea. 
(Components of the female athlete triad).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): [can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea)]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which drug class is utilized cyclically to manage bone resorption in pediatric brittle bone disease?
back: Bisphosphonates. They reduce bone resorption and turnover, decreasing pain and fracture rates while promoting mobility.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 615 (Book Page): [Cyclical bisphosphonate treatment decreases bone resorption and turnover. This reduces bone pain and the fracture rate, promoting weight-bearing mobility and bone strength]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Identify the most common osteoporotic fracture pattern seen in older adults' spines.
back: Thoracic wedge compression fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 421 (Book Page): [Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Why is optimizing a patient's 'Host status' (H) critical before treating chronic osteomyelitis?
back: Comorbidities like smoking and diabetes impair tissue healing, significantly reducing the success rate of surgery for bone infections.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 627 (Book Page): [In chronic infection, it is essential to address medical conditions that may impair wound healing (e.g. smoking, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes, steroid use) prior to surgery.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Differentiate the primary risk factors for nutritional rickets versus osteogenesis imperfecta.
back:
Nutritional rickets: Inadequate Vitamin D/calcium intake. 
OI: Qualitative or quantitative abnormalities in collagen production.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page)/615: [In rickets, the primary problem is inadequate mineralisation of growing bone... OI represents a spectrum of conditions linked by a qualitative and/or quantitative abnormality of collagen production.]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How do mechanical compressive forces affect growth in a weakened immature skeleton?
back: According to the Hueter-Volkmann principle, compressive forces inhibit growth, which can lead to progressive deformity in fragile bones.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 631 (Book Page): [Table 44.1: Hueter-Volkmann principle: Compressive forces inhibit growth; Tensile forces stimulate growth]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: List three systemic host factors that slow the healing process of osteoporotic bones.
back:
1. Diabetes mellitus.
2. Smoking.
3. Peripheral vascular disease.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 451 (Book Page): [Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union), diminished blood supply (peripheral vascular disease...)... smoking]

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Define the primary pathological hallmark of osteoporosis.
back: A condition characterized by low bone mineral density and reduced strength, making bone liable to low-energy fractures.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What are the three components of the 'female athlete triad' that elevate osteoporosis risk?
back:
1. Osteoporosis
2. Disordered eating
3. Amenorrhoea
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): ...female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Contrast the bone failure mechanism in osteoporotic patients versus healthy adults.
back: Osteoporotic bone fails under low-energy loads (e.g., falls from standing height), whereas healthy bone typically requires significant energy transfer.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: An 80-year-old with low bone density sustains a hip fracture. Why is rigid fixation for immediate weight-bearing critical?
back: To avoid the systemic risks of prolonged bed rest and to compensate for pre-existing mobility problems that prevent partial weight-bearing.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): As there may be additional and pre-existing mobility problems, such patients are unable to partially weight-bear and so fixation should be strong enough to allow immediate weight-bearing and to hold the position until union.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Identify the most common metabolic risk factor for inadequate bone mineralization in pediatric populations.
back: Nutritional deficiency, specifically the reduced intake of vitamin D and calcium.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page): Nutritional: Reduced intake of vitamin D and calcium. Environmental: Inadequate exposure to sunlight.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which specific pharmacological group is a risk factor for both avascular necrosis and secondary bone weakening?
back: Corticosteroids.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 619 (Book Page): Causes of avascular necrosis of the femoral head: Steroids; Perthes’ disease; Sickle cell disease; Hypothyroidism.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: According to Wolff’s Law, how does sedentary lifestyle or paralysis increase osteoporosis risk?
back: Bone deposition depends on mechanical stresses; lack of stress (disuse) leads to increased bone resorption and fragility.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 609 (Book Page): Wolff’s law: Bone deposition and resorption depend on the stresses applied. Page 404 (Book Page): Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Differentiate the skeletal defect in Rickets from that of Osteoporosis.
back:
Rickets: Inadequate mineralization of growing bone. 
Osteoporosis: Low bone mineral density and reduced overall strength.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 614 (Book Page): In rickets, the primary problem is inadequate mineralisation of growing bone. Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How do comorbidities like smoking and diabetes act as risk factors for osteoporotic fracture outcomes?
back: They double the time to union and significantly impair biological tissue healing at the fracture site.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 430 (Book Page): Well-known factors that slow down bone healing include diabetes mellitus (doubles time to union), diminished blood supply... smoking... and infection.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Identify the most common clinical site for osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in the elderly.
back: The thoracic spine.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group [Thoracic spine].

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which age group is primarily at risk for osteoporotic wedge compression fractures?
back: - Older adults
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 399 (Book Page): Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What is the inevitable consequence of disuse following a spinal cord injury regarding bone health?
back: - Disuse osteoporosis
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 404 (Book Page): Disuse osteoporosis is an inevitable consequence of spinal cord injury and fragility fractures may occur.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What three risk factors constitute the "female athlete triad"?
back:
1. Osteoporosis
2. Disordered eating
3. Amenorrhoea
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): Stress fractures are also found in female dancers as a result of repetitive training and can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Which specific endocrine factor in female athletes contributes directly to osteoporosis risk?
back: - Amenorrhoea
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What are the two defining quantitative markers of osteoporotic bone?
back:
1. Low bone mineral density
2. Reduced strength
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: In which specific athletic population is repetitive training a high risk factor for stress fractures?
back: - Female dancers
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): Stress fractures are also found in female dancers as a result of repetitive training and can be more frequent in the female athlete triad

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: What nutritional risk factor is identified as part of the female athlete triad leading to bone loss?
back: - Disordered eating
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: How do "low-energy injuries" relate to osteoporotic bone clinical presentation?
back: - Osteoporotic bone is highly liable to fracture from low-energy impacts (e.g., falls from standing height).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height).

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: List two systemic comorbidities that impair bone biology and should be optimized in orthopaedic patients.
back:
1. Smoking
2. Corticosteroid use
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 625 (Book Page): address medical conditions that may impair wound healing (e.g. smoking, peripheral vascular disease, diabetes, steroid use) prior to surgery.

category: Discuss risk factors for osteoporosis
front: Q: Why are female dancers at a distinct risk for stress fractures compared to other athletes?
back: - Combination of repetitive training and elements of the female athlete triad (nutritional/hormonal deficits).
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 507 (Book Page): Stress fractures are also found in female dancers as a result of repetitive training and can be more frequent in the female athlete triad (osteoporosis, disordered eating and amenorrhoea).

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What are the four most common anatomical sites for osteoporotic fractures in elderly patients?
back:
1. Hip (proximal femur)
2. Thoracic spine (T1-T10)
3. Ribs
4. Distal femur
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): "An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture, multiple rib fractures..." Page 420 (Book Page): "Thoracic spine (T1–T10) Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group." Page 437 (Book Page): "Metaphyseal osteoporotic fractures of the distal femur."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why do osteoporotic bones typically fail under "low-energy" mechanisms like a fall from standing height?
back:
• Low bone mineral density
• Reduced structural strength
• Increased brittleness makes bone unable to withstand normal physiological loads.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 443 (Book Page): "Osteoporosis is a condition characterised by low bone mineral density and reduced strength. Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries (e.g. a fall from standing height)."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Contrast the radiographic hallmark of an osteoporotic thoracic fracture with a traumatic Burst fracture.
back:
• Osteoporotic: Wedge compression (anterior collapse).
• Burst fracture: Comminuted failure of the entire vertebral body with interpedicular widening.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): "Thoracic spine (T1–T10) Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group." Page 401 (Book Page): "Burst fractures are comminuted fractures of the vertebral body. They are characterised by widening of the distance between the pedicles."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: An 80-year-old falls from a chair; she is hemodynamically stable. What two common osteoporotic fracture sites must be radiographically excluded despite "appearing well"?
back:
1. Hip fracture
2. Multiple rib fractures
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 375 (Book Page): "An older adult patient falling down a few steps can easily sustain a hip fracture, multiple rib fractures... At frst glance the patient can appear well, but their injury severity score (ISS) and potential mortality could easily exceed those of a younger patient."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: How is a symptomatic osteoporotic wedge fracture of the thoracic spine managed when conservative measures fail?
back: Percutaneous bone cement augmentation, specifically vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): "Symptomatic [osteoporotic wedge] fractures can be treated with percutaneous bone cement augmentation, known as vertebroplasty or kyphoplasty."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: What classic clinical triad describes the presentation of an osteoporotic proximal femoral fracture?
back:
1. Shortened limb
2. Externally rotated leg
3. Inability to weight-bear after a low-energy fall.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 418 (Book Page): "A shortened externally rotated leg in an older patient suggests a fracture of the proximal femur." Page 443 (Book Page): "Osteoporotic bone is liable to fracture with low-energy injuries."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: Why is the "medial calcar" significant in the mechanical stability of osteoporotic extracapsular hip fractures?
back: Comminution of the medial calcar (lesser trochanter) creates an unstable environment that resists compression and often requires an intramedullary nail for relative stability.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 437 (Book Page): "Unstable fractures include... where the medial calcar is a comminuted (lesser trochanter) fracture... an intramedullary device might be considered."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: A patient with known osteoporosis presents with back pain after lifting a bag. X-ray shows wedging at T8. What is the diagnosis?
back: Osteoporotic wedge compression fracture.
citation: In book "Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery", Page 420 (Book Page): "Thoracic spine (T1–T10) Osteoporotic wedge compression fractures in older adults are the commonest injury in this group."

category: Identify common sites of osteoporotic fractures
front: Q: How does the "sliding screw" in a Dynamic Hip Screw (DHS) accommodate the settling of osteoporotic bone?
back: It allows for controlled impaction and compression at the fracture site while preventing the screw from penetrating the femoral head as the weak bone settles.
